newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty softens vs basket, seen range bound.
newsitem.headline: Zloty softens vs basket, seen range bound.

text.p: The Polish zloty eased some 0.2 points against the basket of currencies in early trade on foreign investor currency buying and then stabilized at around minus 0.65 percent from parity for the rest of the day.
Dealers said that in the near-term the zloty would remain locked within a range set over the last days and continue to track dollar/mark movements amid thin summer holiday trading.
"The zloty should be traded between -0.3 and -1.0 percent for now," said Wojciech Trzepizur, forex dealer at BRE SA.
The zloty closed down at -0.66/-0.71 percent from the trading band centre against Monday's -0.40/-0.48 percent close.
It closed at 3.4840/55 to the dollar, down from 3.4650/00 on Monday and at 1.8550/65 to the mark, down from 1.8545/55.

Dealers said that a bearish longer-term zloty outlook and uncertainty over parliamentary elections in late September have kept larger speculative foreign capital from flowing into the country despite a hefty official interest rate rise on Monday.
One-day rates slipped further on the cash-heavy money market as the central bank again did not offer any open market operations to soak up excess liquidity, dealers said.
Overnight rates ended at 23.30/24.00 percent, down from Monday's 24.10/24.60 percent.

Tomorrow/next rates were at 23.35/23.90 percent against yesterday's close at 24.50/24.70. Few investors were expected to bid at Wednesday's one billion zloty fixed two- and five-year T-bond auction because the finance ministry was unlikely to raise its yields to match those on the secondary market despite a central bank rate rise.

Analysts said the ministry could cap 15-percent two-year bonds yields around 22.35 percent against secondary market quotes around 23.65. Even less interest was expected in the 12-percent five-year paper as it was seen as illiquid.
